what_its_for: This medication is a combination birth control pill used to prevent pregnancy. It contains two female hormones — a progestin (norethindrone) and an estrogen (ethinyl estradiol) — that work together to stop ovulation (the release of an egg), thicken cervical mucus to keep sperm from reaching an egg, and thin the uterine lining. The iron tablets included in the pack help replace iron you may lose during your period. This pill may also help make your periods more regular, lighter, and less painful, and can sometimes improve acne.
how_to_take: Take one tablet by mouth every day at the same time each day. Your pill pack contains active hormone pills (usually white or light-colored) and reminder iron tablets (usually brown or dark-colored). Take the active pills first in order, then take the iron tablets during the last 7 days of your pack. Start a new pack the very next day after finishing your current pack — do not skip any days between packs. Swallow the tablet whole with or without food. If the pill upsets your stomach, try taking it with food or at bedtime. Use a backup method of contraception (such as condoms) for the first 7 days if you are just starting this pill for the first time.
dosing: Take one pill every day for 28 days. Most packs contain 21 active hormone pills followed by 7 iron (reminder) pills. Take the pills in the exact order shown on the pack. Your period will usually come during the week you are taking the iron reminder pills. Start each new pack on the same day of the week as your first pack, without any break between packs.
missed_dose: If you miss 1 active pill: Take it as soon as you remember, even if it means taking 2 pills in one day. Then continue taking your pills at your regular time. No backup birth control is needed. If you miss 2 active pills in a row in Week 1 or Week 2: Take 2 pills on the day you remember and 2 pills the next day, then finish the rest of the pack as usual. Use a backup method (like condoms) for 7 days. If you miss 2 active pills in a row in Week 3, or if you miss 3 or more active pills in a row at any time: Throw out the rest of the pack and start a new pack the same day. Use backup birth control for 7 days. You may not get your period this month — this is expected. If you miss any of the 7 brown iron reminder pills, just throw them away and keep taking one pill per day. You do not need backup birth control for missing iron pills. If you are unsure what to do, use a backup method and call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep away from moisture, heat, and direct sunlight. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep this medication out of reach of children and pets. Do not use pills past the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid smoking, especially if you are 35 years of age or older. Smoking while taking birth control pills greatly increases your risk of serious heart and blood vessel problems, including heart attack and stroke. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as it may affect how this medication works. Avoid taking antacids, calcium supplements, or dairy products at the same time as your iron tablets, as they can reduce iron absorption — try to take iron tablets on an empty stomach if possible, or at least 1 to 2 hours apart from these foods and products. Tell all of your doctors and your pharmacist about every medication you take, including herbal supplements. Some medications can make birth control pills less effective, such as rifampin (an antibiotic), certain seizure medications (like phenytoin or carbamazepine), and St. John's Wort herbal supplement.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience any of the following warning signs — remember the acronym ACHES: Abdominal pain (severe), Chest pain or shortness of breath, Headache (severe or sudden), Eye problems (blurred vision, loss of vision), Severe leg pain or swelling (especially in the calf). Also contact your doctor if you have: yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), signs of depression or mood changes, unusual vaginal bleeding, breast lumps, migraines that are new or getting worse, high blood pressure, or if you think you might be pregnant. Tell your doctor right away if you have not had a period for two months in a row.
when_it_works: If you start taking this pill on the first day of your period, it works right away to prevent pregnancy. If you start on any other day, it may take up to 7 days to become effective — use a backup method like condoms during this time. For other benefits like lighter periods or improved acne, it may take 2 to 3 months of regular use before you notice a difference. It is very important to take the pill every day at the same time to get the best protection.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do not use this medication if you are pregnant or think you might be pregnant. Stop taking it immediately if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: This combination pill is generally not recommended for women who are breastfeeding, especially in the first 6 weeks after delivery, as it may reduce your milk supply. Talk to your doctor about alternatives. Teenagers: This medication can be used by teenagers after their first menstrual period. No dose adjustment is needed. Older adults: This medication is not typically used after menopause. Women over 35 who smoke should not use this medication due to a significantly increased risk of serious cardiovascular events. Liver disease: This medication should not be used if you have current or past liver disease or liver tumors. Talk to your doctor for a safe alternative.
